extracted.intended_audience: writers seeking literary agents (users of #MSWL / ManuscriptWishList)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical instructions for searching #MSWL (Manuscript Wish List) tweets and the ManuscriptWishList.com site to identify literary agents who are a good fit for your manuscript. Focuses on search techniques, keywords, and site features to generate a list of agents to query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try as many search options as you can
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend you try as many search options as you can – then make a large list of which agent(s) to query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be exhaustive in searching across tools and filters before narrowing down; generate a large list of potential agents rather than relying on a few hits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Twitter Advanced Search with #MSWL in the hashtags field
rubrics_metrics.description: Type in #MSWL in the “these hashtags” field on Twitter’s Advanced Search page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine the hashtag filter with other keywords in the top fields to zero in on relevant wishlist tweets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Twitter using targeted keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: When using Twitter Advanced Search, include keywords such as titles of books/TV/movies similar to your work, your genre (written out and abbreviated), tropes, and names of historical figures (for historical fiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: similar works like Stranger Things; genre both 'young adult' and 'YA'; tropes like 'friends to lovers'. Use multiple keyword variants to capture different wordings agents might use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the ManuscriptWishList.com genre search and check all applicable boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Head to the genre search page on ManuscriptWishList.com and check all of the boxes that could apply to your work to generate the most leads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting every applicable category increases the number of potential matches; be generous when in doubt to maximize results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure you select 'Agent' and applicable genres before searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure to click 'Agent,' those applicable genres, and hit Search to see a list of people who may be a good fit for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to select 'Agent' or correct genres will filter out relevant results—confirm these selections before running searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the keyword search bar on the site as an alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: You can also search simply by keyword in the keyword search bar on the right of ManuscriptWishList.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a quicker, more freeform way to find agents by typing concise keywords rather than using multiple checkbox filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open agent profiles and view their #MSWL tweets
rubrics_metrics.description: After finding agents on ManuscriptWishList.com, open their full profile and click the button that shows that agent’s #MSWL tweets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read those tweets to confirm that the agent's stated wishlist actually matches your project before deciding to query them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use examples of similar works to guide search choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use titles of books, TV shows, and movies similar to your work (e.g., Stranger Things) as search keywords or to check relevant genre/trope boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using well-known comparable titles helps locate agents interested in similar tones/themes; cross-reference those results with agent tweets/profiles for fit.
